license_scope: Original DVIDIA catalog and procedural shoes only; robot simulation assets retain their individual licenses.
scope: Reusable native scene assets with synthetic rigid shoes. Scene loading and gravity/contact checks do not demonstrate shoe manipulation, learning or physical robot transfer.
world_frame: right-handed; robot base reference at world origin, +z up

robots.name: UR5e + Robotiq 2F-85
robots.gripper_command: Native coupled gripper servo input [0,255]; not a measured gap or calibrated force.

source.verification: Packaged SHA256 allowlist; assets are read from verified bytes, without network access.
source.home_scope: Authored scene initialization: UR5e and PiPER use the upstream home arm pose, zero gripper coordinates; SO101 uses its zero reference pose.

compatibility.scope: Pinned native arm and gripper can share a rigid-shoe scene. This does not establish reachability, graspability, a shoe manipulation skill, or hardware compatibility.

robots.openness_scope: These licenses cover pinned simulation assets; SDK and physical hardware design licenses are separate.

environment.name: asset_table
environment.default_layout: Three columns x=.40,.76,1.12 m; two rows y=.38,.56 m; sole bottoms begin z=.08 m. Layout separates loading tests from reachability claims.

limitations: All shoe physical properties are untested synthetic assumptions.
Left/right labels identify mirrored procedural instances, not scanned real shoes.
Arm command interfaces differ; installing a scene does not install a learned controller.
No deformation, real-world calibration, graspability claim or closed-loop sensor stack.
